title: 围岩裂隙精准识别与三维模型重构
visual_status: ORIGINAL 68-PAGE PDF ALL-PAGE CONTACT-SHEET AUDIT; 68 rendered pages / 12 contact sheets

problem_data_contract.independent_evaluation_unit: Q1: original borehole unfolded image/depth segment; Q2: image-level fracture instance/trace; Q3: ordered physical fracture centerline/profile; Q4: fracture pair / 3D spatial grid point / candidate borehole location
problem_data_contract.input_structure: four attachment families of borehole wall unfolded images; pixel-to-mm calibration; sinusoidal traces; roughness profiles; six known borehole coordinates/depths
problem_data_contract.validation_priority: Q1 must establish provenance of manual/reference masks and split at original image/borehole level; Q2 compare fit methods on independent images/traces with physical period contract; Q3 separate numerical convergence from physical ground truth; Q4 distinguish heuristic spatial scores from calibrated probabilities/posterior uncertainty and enforce all engineering constraints against existing and newly proposed boreholes
problem_data_contract.author_evaluation_scope: selected attachment images, pixel confusion counts for three Q1 images, aggregate Q2 comparison table without named statistical-test protocol, numerical JRC sampling comparisons, and heuristic Q4 connectivity/coverage optimization; code is referenced as Attachment 9 but not included in the available excellent-paper ZIP/PDF

questions.Q1: two-stage fracture segmentation: six classical detectors vote for coarse localization, then 12 connected-component features are manually scored with threshold 6/10
questions.Q2: DBSCAN + horizontal-band merge + RANSAC/least-squares sinusoid versus sliding-window reduced-Hough model; estimate R/P/beta/C
questions.Q3: Fourier main contour + four-level DWT detail decomposition + Bootstrap + four sampling schemes + area-roughness-corrected JRC
questions.Q4: 2D-to-3D fracture reconstruction, multiplicative five-factor connectivity score, DFS clusters, distance-decay information coverage surrogate, greedy supplementary-borehole placement

evidence: original 68-page PDF visually audited through 68 page renders / 12 contact sheets
formulas, tables, pseudocode and result surfaces statically audited
not_achieved: R2: Appendix A only states 'Attachment 9: code for each question'; the available excellent-paper collection contains PDFs only and does not provide Attachment 9 source code for static audit
R3-R7: no executable author code/data chain, end-to-end reproduction or independent transfer is available

key_strengths: Q1 makes low-label classical image processing a serious route rather than assuming deep learning and exposes a transparent two-stage coarse-to-fine architecture
Q2 explicitly compares two model families and uses DBSCAN/RANSAC to address fragmented/noisy sinusoidal traces
Q3 recognizes that roughness estimates depend on sampling density and compares equal, curvature, gradient and entropy-driven sampling
Q4 links geometry, network connectivity, spatial coverage and measurement placement into a complete decision narrative
key_risks: Q1 Table 5 gives TP/FP/FN/TN and strong Precision/Recall/F1 but the paper does not state how ground-truth fracture pixels were created, by whom, or whether the 12-feature scoring weights/threshold were tuned independently of the three evaluated images
Q1 manual 12-feature reward weights and threshold 6/10 are acknowledged as subjective in section 7.1; no learned-weight or held-out threshold calibration is demonstrated
Q2 model description says RANSAC estimates R/P/beta/C, but pseudocode Step3 names only Rinit/betainit/Cinit before Step9 outputs P; the period-estimation primitive is underspecified
Q2 horizontal-band merge is described as horizontal distance but Eq.35 uses |yA-yB|; semantic axis/distance contract is inconsistent

Q2 reduced-Hough model fixes P to reduce dimension, while model-one Table 7 reports freely varying P values from 80 to 110 mm even though the cylindrical physical period should be tied to circumference when geometry is known
Q2 Table 6 reports p<0.01/0.01 for five metrics but provides no statistical test name, statistic, sample unit, pairing rule or sample size; significance provenance is not auditable

Q3 Bootstrap pseudocode says the main model uses least squares but Step3 switches to maximum likelihood; percentile CI is printed as [theta_(1-a/2), theta_(a/2)], reversed for conventional lower/upper order
Q3 calls high-density convergence 'true JRC' although no independent physical roughness ground truth is shown; convergence of estimators is numerical-reference evidence, not accuracy truth
Q3 enhanced JRC coefficients alpha=0.15±0.03 and beta=0.02±0.01 are stated without a visible calibration dataset/estimation method; treat as heuristic until provenance exists
Q3/Q4 range contract drifts: Q3 sampling values are around 17-40 and Q4 reports JRC 25-60 (including values exactly 60), while connectivity uses JRCmax=20 as a similarity scale without justification

Q4 Pc=Pd*Po*Pz*PJRC*Pt is called connectivity probability based on conditional-independence language, but the factor functions and scales are heuristic and no labeled connectivity calibration is shown
Q4 average network statement conflicts across surfaces: abstract says 32/50=64% isolated, while body says about 85% have no connectivity; both cannot denote the same isolation rate

Q4 cluster 12 reports mean connectivity 0.196 while the edge threshold is 0.3; this can be valid only if the table averages all within-cluster pairs rather than retained graph edges, but the aggregation denominator is not defined

Q4 'uncertainty' is generated from distance-decayed information coverage plus IDW rather than a stated random-variable posterior; it is a spatial coverage surrogate unless a probabilistic observation/update model is added
Q4 'information gain' is the reduction of that deterministic coverage surrogate after adding a candidate; it is not expected information gain over possible observations

Q4 the 500 mm spacing text is broader than the mathematical constraint: Eq.71 only constrains pairs of new holes. All three proposed new holes are >500 mm apart, but (800,1300) is only about 424.3 mm from existing hole 4 at (500,1000); if the safety rule applies to all boreholes, the formal model omits an existing-vs-new feasibility constraint
Q4 the claimed 0.523 to 0.395 reduction replays to 24.474%, consistent with the stated 24.5% after rounding, but no code/data artifact is available to reproduce the fields themselves

Paper Appendix A references eleven external attachments including Attachment 9 code, but those artifacts are absent from the available source package; visual completeness is therefore not implementation completeness
applicable_conditions: low-label borehole fracture image extraction where transparent classical filters are useful
periodic fracture traces on calibrated cylindrical unfolded images
roughness estimation from an ordered physical centerline with sampling-sensitivity analysis
exploratory spatial coverage and drilling recommendation when heuristic assumptions are labeled as such
failure_or_abandon_conditions: Q1 ground-truth mask provenance is unknown or the scoring threshold is tuned/evaluated on the same images without holdout
Q2 period or amplitude violates known borehole geometry and the method has no reject state
Q3 adaptive sampling is declared more accurate merely because it converges to a dense-sampling reference without external truth
Q4 heuristic compatibility/coverage outputs are interpreted as calibrated probability/posterior uncertainty, or safety spacing is not checked against all relevant existing/new holes
recommended_redo: Q1 keep six-filter/connected-component pipeline as a 6-hour no-label baseline, but replace manual scoring weights with a small interpretable classifier if labels exist; freeze original-image/borehole split before weight/threshold fitting and publish mask provenance

Q2 use topology-aware instance grouping then fit y=R*sin(2*pi*x/P+beta)+C with P fixed to pi*D when D is known; use bounded robust least-squares/RANSAC+refit, canonical phase, residual diagnostics and reject logic; compare sliding-window/Hough only under the same independent trace split

Q3 extract one ordered centerline in millimetres, freeze one canonical JRC formula, report sampling convergence relative to a declared numerical reference rather than truth, and calibrate any area correction on separate data before recommendation

Q4 use geometry-derived compatibility score unless connectivity labels justify probability calibration; represent uncertainty as an explicit stochastic posterior or call it coverage score; formulate candidate utility as expected posterior reduction only when an observation model exists; enforce new-new and existing-new hard spacing before ranking
